feed.title: Field Notes
feed.subtitle: Short notes on keeping a field notebook, written as the season goes.

entry.title: What to write down
entry.summary: The five things every entry records, and why the weather is one of them.
entry.content:
Every entry records the same five things, in the same order, so that a page read a year later answers its own questions.

date      2026-10-02
place     north meadow, by the gate
weather   overcast, light wind from the west
who       Sam, Ali
seen      two kestrels hunting the bank

The weather matters more than it seems: half of what you will not see is explained by it. Write it as you find it, and keep <b>tags</b> & symbols out of your head: this page shows them as you typed them.

Abbreviations

Keep a list of your abbreviations on the inside cover, and never change what one means.

entry.title: Starting a field notebook
entry.summary: Why a paper notebook still beats a phone outdoors, and the one rule that keeps it useful.
entry.content:
A field notebook is a record you can trust later, written at the moment you saw something. It does not need batteries, it does not mind rain, and nobody has ever lost an afternoon's notes to a software update.

The one rule

Write the date and the place first, every time, before anything else. An observation without a when and a where is a story, not a record.

What to carry

  • a notebook with numbered pages
  • a pencil, which writes on damp paper
  • a ruler marked in millimetres
